en: Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for its perfect conical shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the sea.
The Philippine eagle is the national bird and a critically endangered species endemic to the tropical forests of Mindanao.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a unique freshwater lake located entirely within the main crater of an active volcano.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Luzon is the largest and most populous island in the Philippine archipelago, located in the northern part of the country.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected marine sanctuary known for its pristine coral biodiversity.
The Philippines experiences a tropical climate characterized by a wet southwest monsoon season called habagat and a dry northeast monsoon.
The abaca plant, native to the Philippines, produces a highly durable natural fiber used globally to make specialty papers and ropes.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly through a cave into the sea.
The Philippines sits along the Pacific Ring of Fire, a major tectonic boundary that causes frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
